experiment: For each of the 150 successful persisted campaign block/wavelength retrievals, keep the native 7.5 m grid, measured RCS, productive reference altitude and assumed aerosol lidar ratio fixed. Recompute deterministic backward KFS with beta_total(ref)=beta_m(ref)*(1+f), where f is a declared sensitivity parameter rather than an inferred aerosol fraction. Compare each f>0 result with the otherwise identical f=0 deterministic solution over 0.6-6 km.
important_semantics: This is a sensitivity envelope, not an estimate or prior for real beta_aer(ref).
Relative changes can be large when the f=0 aerosol column is small; they quantify dependence on the boundary assumption, not observational truth error.
No f value is proposed as a threshold, correction or productive uncertainty model.
interpretation: The campaign retrieval is highly sensitive to the aerosol-free reference assumption even at the existing productive reference altitudes: f=0.02 changes the lower-column solution by about 5% in median across the campaign, and f=0.05 by about 14%.
This does not imply that real residual fractions are 0.02 or 0.05. It demonstrates that beta_aer(ref) is a scientifically material nuisance parameter if it is not observationally constrained.
The sensitivity exists before any high-column boundary move or vertical aggregation, reinforcing that boundary-condition uncertainty is conceptually distinct from high-altitude signal support.
decision: Keep boundary residual aerosol as an explicit assumption/sensitivity dimension in P5.4 R&D. Do not silently absorb it into Rayleigh shape QA, SNR or vertical aggregation uncertainty.
